Integral conservation means d/dt ∫ from x_1 to x_2 of q(x,t) dx = f(q(x_1,t)) − f(q(x_2,t)); the accompanying interpretation is that the amount inside an interval changes only through flux past its endpoints [raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, Section 1.1.1, equation (1.10) and following paragraph].

contract_plain_english: Variable-coefficient hyperbolic equations need not have conservation form. The book therefore develops wave-propagation methods with broader applicability, using waves from Riemann problems directly. For conservation laws these methods have a natural, subsequently explained connection to standard flux-differencing methods. Many shock-capturing ideas extend beyond conservation laws, and the author aims to present that broader framework and its less traditional applications. These are the claims of the selected paragraph; it supplies no explicit nonconservative equation, flux-obstruction theorem, or mass-production calculation [raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, Section 1.4, paragraph beginning 'Hyperbolic equations with variable coefficients'].
